findings.summary: The player (teal trapezoid) and every threat/wall segment (pink rectangles) are flat, untextured primitive shapes with no finished art applied, visible in every frame.
On mobile the onboarding/instruction subtitle wraps under the floating Pause button and is partly hidden behind it; recurs in most mobile frames outside the paused/loss screens.
The scene above the horizon line is a flat black void with no scenery, props or lighting beyond thin grid lines, leaving most of the frame empty on both viewports.
The crashed debris chunk is rendered with pseudo-3D isometric shading (angled top face, darker side), inconsistent with the flat 2D rectangles used for player and obstacles everywhere else.

states.comment: Player trapezoid and a threat rectangle sit on an empty void with grid-line horizon; the subtitle clearly states the objective and the Pause button is fully visible.
Same flat shapes and empty void as desktop, but the wrapped subtitle text runs under the Pause button, partially obscuring it.
Multiple pink obstacle rectangles and the teal player trapezoid are visible and distinguishable by colour; HUD is unobstructed.
Same stacked obstacle rectangles as desktop; the subtitle text is again partly covered by the Pause button.
Pause overlay with glowing 'Paused' text and a styled Resume button reads clearly; steer before/after frames show the same flat entities moving with no overlap issues.
The Paused/Resume screen itself is clean and legible, but the steer and pre-pause frames still show the subtitle text obscured by the Pause button.
'Crashed', final Score/Best and a 'Race again' button are clearly legible against the dark background, though faded obstacle rectangles and an oddly-shaded debris cube linger behind the text.
Loss state matches desktop: clear 'Crashed' headline, score, and a well-sized touch-friendly 'Race again' button with no overlap.

look_reason: Every entity is an untextured flat rectangle/trapezoid on an empty black void with only grid lines for a horizon, which reads as a programmer-art placeholder build rather than a finished, publishable game.
